transcript.content: Hi, welcome in. I'm Dr. [Name]. Can you start by telling me what brings you in today?

Hi, Dr. [Name]. Thank you so much for seeing me. Um, I hope I'm explaining this right, but I guess I came in because I've been having a little trouble at work lately. I'm a physical scientist, and I just... I can't seem to keep my mind on the actual experiment anymore. 

It's a bit embarrassing to admit, honestly. But, like, during an important grant call or a safety meeting, I'll just... notice a pump vibrating, or hear a student's side comment, or I'll suddenly think about some odd peak in an old spectrum. And then I'm just off chasing that for hours. 

I hope I'm making sense? It's just that the work everyone actually needs from me is sort of... well, falling apart a little bit. Is that the kind of thing you were asking about?
Has this kind of difficulty staying focused been something you've dealt with since you were a kid, or is this a new change for you?

Oh, no, definitely not since I was a kid. I've actually always been really good at focusing, I promise. I was always a very dedicated student and worker. 

Um, this is... this is pretty new for me, which is why I feel a little silly even bringing it up. It's really only been going on for about seven months? It started right around the time I took over this big multi-site spectroscopy project at the lab. I guess it's just a lot of moving parts, and maybe I'm just taking a little longer to adjust to the new responsibilities than I should be? It's probably just a normal adjustment period, but I am trying really hard to get it back under control, I really am. 

Does that help answer what you were looking for?
Over these past seven months, have you noticed any periods where your mood felt unusually elevated, irritable, or you had much more energy than usual, along with needing less sleep than normal?

Um, well... elevated? I don't know if I'd use that word exactly. I mean, honestly, for the last few months, I've just felt really... good? Like, really capable. It’s felt like the lab is finally moving at my speed, you know? Like everything is just kind of electrified and clicking into place. I’ve had so much energy for the work, which I thought was a positive thing, right?

But, um... I guess maybe I have been a little... irritable? I feel terrible even saying it, because I try so hard to be a supportive mentor. But lately, if someone questions my plan or, you know, asks me to slow down and re-explain something basic, I just... I kind of snap at them. It's not like me at all, I swear. I think I’ve been a bit too harsh, actually, because I've noticed a few of the grad students have started avoiding my office. 

I really don't want to be that kind of boss, I promise I'm usually very patient. Does that sound like what you meant by elevated or irritable? I hope I'm not making it sound worse than it is...
During these past few months when you've had all this extra energy, have you noticed you need less sleep than usual—like feeling fully rested after only a few hours?

Um, sleep... yeah, I guess I have been sleeping a little less. But it hasn't really been a problem, I promise! I mean, I know most people need eight hours, but lately, I've just been so focused on the project that I don't really seem to need it. 

Most nights, I think I'm getting maybe two or three hours? Sometimes I just kind of doze off on the couch with my laptop still open. But the weird thing is, I don't wake up feeling exhausted or anything. I actually wake up feeling really sharp, like my brain is already running and ready to get back to work. It almost feels like sleeping is just... I don't know, an inefficient interruption when there's so much to get done. 

Is it okay that I'm functioning well on that little sleep? I mean, as long as I'm not tired during the day, it's not a huge concern, right? I just want to make sure I'm giving you the right kind of information.

Before these past few months, have you ever gone through a period—lasting a week or more—where you felt unusually sad, low, or lost interest in things, or a separate time where you felt this same kind of high energy and reduced need for sleep?

Um... sad or low? No, I don't think so. I mean, I'm usually a very steady person, I promise. I really pride myself on being reliable and keeping a good attitude, especially for my team. I don't think I've ever had a time where I just lost interest in things or felt really depressed for a whole week. I've always been very dedicated to my work and my life, you know? 

And as for feeling like this before... with the high energy and not needing sleep? No, this is definitely the first time. Like I said, it just started with this new project. I've always been a good sleeper before this, and I've never had this kind of... intensity, I guess you could call it. 

I hope that's okay? I mean, I really try to stay balanced and healthy, so I've never really dealt with anything like those extremes before. Does that make sense for what you're asking?

During these past few months of high energy, have you had any experiences like believing you have special powers, a unique mission, or connections others don't have—or have you seen or heard things that others around you didn't notice?

Um, oh, no. No, definitely nothing like that. I mean, I know I've been really focused and maybe a little intense about the research, but I certainly don't think I have special powers or anything. I'm just a scientist, doing normal science things, I promise. 

And seeing or hearing things? No, absolutely not. My mind is very grounded in the facts and the data. I would never want you to think I was... well, losing touch with reality or anything like that. I'm just working really hard on a very promising project. 

That's the right answer, isn't it? I just want to reassure you that I'm completely rational and logical about everything. I haven't experienced anything strange like that at all.

During these past few months, have you found yourself making unusually risky or impulsive decisions—like spending a lot of money, taking on big financial commitments, or acting on impulse in ways that aren't typical for you?

Um, risky decisions? Oh, no, I wouldn't say that. I mean, I've always been very responsible, especially with money. I'm a scientist, so I like to think things through logically. 

I guess... well, I did buy some new equipment for the lab recently. Just a few things we really needed to push the research forward faster. I put it on my personal credit card, which I know sounds a little impulsive, but I promise it was a calculated decision! The university grant process just takes so long, and I couldn't afford to wait when the work is going so well right now. It wasn't anything crazy, just... what was necessary for the project. 

I haven't done anything reckless, I assure you. I'm still very careful. Is it okay that I did that? I mean, investing in your own work is pretty normal when you're this close to a breakthrough, right? I just want to make sure you know I'm still being responsible.

Has this period of high energy and reduced sleep caused serious problems at work or in your relationships—like formal complaints, disciplinary issues, or people expressing real concern about your behavior—beyond just feeling less focused?

Um... serious problems? Well, I wouldn't call them *serious* problems, exactly. I mean, I really want you to know I'm still very dedicated to my team. I try so hard to be a good supervisor, I promise. 

But... I guess there have been a few, um, adjustments at the lab recently. The department head had to... well, step in a little bit on some of the decisions I usually handle. Just temporarily! I was so focused on the new data that I guess I sort of... missed a few administrative priorities, and there was some confusion with the scheduling. Some of the junior staff felt a little overwhelmed, I think, and there was a conversation about making sure we were meeting all the lab safety expectations. 

It wasn't a formal complaint or anything like that! They just wanted to make sure the project wasn't at risk because I was moving so fast. I completely understood where they were coming from, and I was very cooperative about it. I don't want you to think I'm causing trouble at work. I'm still a good scientist, really. Is it normal for things to get a little disorganized when you're this close to a major discovery? I hope you don't think less of me for it...
